citation: 1827 S. Prairie [John W. Doane residence]. Unknown photographer, undated (after the house's completion in late 1882). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 1827 S. Prairie; the Glessner House Museum's blog reproduces the same photograph ('Electricity comes to Prairie Avenue, 1882', August 2013).
author: unknown photographer
date: undated (after the house's completion in late 1882)
repository: chicagology.com (secondary reproduction; the original holder is not named). Prairie library images cgn-1827-doane-exterior (this copy, 1444 x 1770 px) and a18-gh-doane-exterior (the Glessner House Museum blog's smaller copy of the same photograph), both recorded there as 'link only'; the project's reference copy is the image store's (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/cgn-1827-doane-exterior.jpg), committed since T-3171 at data/sources/assets/doane_1827_photo_t3171/ with its attribution, as the owner directed on 2026-10-11 for the image gate's pictures.
locator: The whole print: the Prairie front on the left, from the porch behind the street tree at its north end (1823's porch beyond it at the left edge) to the south-west corner and its square tower; the south flank on the right, running back past its chimney stacks to the coach house; the iron fence on its stone curb and the public walk across the foot.
rights_note: A secondary web reproduction whose original source and rights are not stated (the Prairie library's own ruling: 'unknown - link only'). Only forms, counts, places and proportions are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset (no texture, no traced mesh), and the copy committed for the image gate (T-3171) is the store's, unaltered, with its attribution in the folder's README.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-26 (T-3171, piece 1 of T-1895) from the image store's reference copy, 1444 x 1770 px greyscale, sha256 64e06383a60fdcc6a68ad1aa32db91dde8d1678f0a671ea1447768f487f5ac13. The library's camera position ('north-west of the house, facing south-east') is not the print's: it looks north-east from the south-west (the folder's README says why).
note: The one photograph of the Doane house this project builds from. It shows a stone house of two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard: the front in coursed ashlar, light and darker courses in turn, with a shallow pavilion carrying three lights a storey under carved hoods and, over the cornice, a steep pyramidal roof with a finial; a window bay south of it under segmental hoods with a pedimented dormer over it; at the south-west corner a block with a narrow cant, carried up a storey past the cornice as a square tower under a tall slated hip with a crested top and two finials; at the front's north end, behind the street tree, a porch on columns with a balustraded balcony and steps; barred basement lights; a moulded stone cornice; two tall stone stacks over the south flank; and along the walk an iron fence of scrolled bars on a stone curb, ending at a stone pier.
what_it_supplies: the front's composition: the pavilion and its lights, the window bay, the porch at the north end, the dormers
the heights of the basement, the storeys, the windows, the cornice and the mansard through the photograph's camera
the corner block, its tower and the pavilion's pyramidal roof (T-3172), and the south flank's stacks
what_it_does_not_supply: the north flank, the rear and the brick rear range
the porch's detail and the door, behind the street tree
